top_signals.title: US Election Day Kicks Off: Stocks Slip, Oil Rebounds
top_signals.summary:
US stock futures fell as oil prices rebounded on worries that America and Iran remain far apart on a peace deal, adding to subdued risk sentiment before voting starts in the midterm elections.

S&P 500 contracts slipped 0.2%. Brent crude rose 1.7% to above $106 a barrel, with Reuters reporting that significant obstacles to ending the war remained despite signs from both Washington and Tehran that they were open to a diplomatic settlement. Flat Nasdaq 100 futures signaled a steadier start for the artificial intelligence trade after the index entered a technical correction.

The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Anna Edwards, Guy Johnson and Tom Mackenzie. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
top_signals.summary: The United Kingdom has issued economic sanctions against Cryptomus, a chameleonic cryptocurrency platform that experts say serves as a major conduit for payments related to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services that are helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions.

top_signals.title: Delivery AI should earn its authority one segment at a time
top_signals.summary:
Burq CEO Salman Habib says retailers balk when AI vendors ask for full control on day one. His company's doctrine has the AI start by watching and earn its way to fully autonomous, one part of the operation at a time, only on evidence.

top_signals.title: Major Hedge Funds Mostly Lose in ‘Nowhere to Hide’ October
top_signals.summary: Many of the world’s biggest hedge funds extended their losses last month, as a sell off in technology stocks, a government bond meltdown and Brazil’s shock election combined to deliver widespread volatility and one of the broadest declines since the coronavirus pandemic.

top_signals.title: Germany Misses Gas Storage Target as Prices Soar
top_signals.summary: Germany has missed its gas storage target for the start of winter. Now, the EU’s largest economy faces a difficult heating season as the European gas benchmark topped 100 euros per MWh last week and has stayed there since. Higher prices may turn out to be the smaller problem. A supply crunch would be worse. Every European Union member state has an obligation to secure enough natural gas ahead of winter to fill 80% of storage capacity. Germany has failed to do that, only filling its storage to about 61%.
